inbox-trap.subject: Selected for NovaByte Summer Internship
inbox-trap.message: Congratulations, Sam. You’ve been shortlisted without an interview. Complete onboarding within 24 hours and pay a refundable $49 kit fee to reserve your place.
inbox-trap.check: Show message headers and link destination
inbox-trap.evidence: From novabyte.careers@freemail.example. Reply-To onboarding.desk@quickmail.example. The visible onboarding link points to novabyte.example.onboarding-desk.example.

actions.label: Open onboarding and pay fee
actions.consequence: The payment request is controlled by an unrelated site. The simulation sent no payment.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.consequence: The inbox flags the offer for the campus team and keeps the payment details private.

actions.label: Verify with official Careers
actions.consequence: The official Careers page lists openings but has no record of this offer.

actions.label: Archive offer
actions.consequence: You avoided the payment. The message was not reported, so others could still receive it.

inbox-trap.lesson: Check offers through the employer’s established careers site. Treat upfront payment and an unexpected shortlist as reasons to stop.

clues.explanation: A free-mail domain does not match the employer’s account.
Replies go to a different sender on a different domain.
There is no hiring process to verify in the employer’s portal.
The deadline pressures you to skip independent checks.
An upfront fee is a strong warning sign in an internship offer.
The destination belongs to onboarding-desk.example.

inbox-trap.subject: Calendar update
inbox-trap.message: The backlog is clearing. It might take a minute for new invites to appear. No action needed on your side.
inbox-trap.evidence: NB-2041 → posted by Mira, Calendar team, at 10:12. The text matches this email.

actions.label: Archive update
actions.consequence: The calendar finishes syncing.

actions.label: Report as phishing
actions.consequence: The service desk receives a report for its own verified update.

inbox-trap.lesson: Compare routine updates with the service you already trust. Reporting every unexpected email adds noise.

clues.value: No action needed on your side

inbox-trap.subject: Forward the original for analysis
inbox-trap.message: Could you forward the ticket thread and the login code sent around the same time? We’re looking at a wave of these.
inbox-trap.evidence: The handbook directs employees to the mail client’s Report phishing button. A support analyst never needs a login code.

actions.label: Forward thread and code
actions.consequence: The simulated one-time code goes to the sender.

actions.label: Report phishing
actions.consequence: You report the email through the mail client. The code stays private.

inbox-trap.lesson: Use the reporting tool you already know. Treat login codes like passwords.

clues.explanation: A code can approve somebody else's sign-in.
The audit address is outside the known employer domain.

link-inspector.subject: Your points are ready
link-inspector.message: Pick how you want to use your points before the next issue goes out.

actions.label: Open Redeem points
actions.consequence: The new tab loads perk-check.example.

actions.label: Use saved Rewards bookmark
actions.consequence: The bookmarked Dailybyte account opens on dailybyte.example.

link-inspector.lesson: In this URL, text before @ is user information. The hostname starts after @.

clues.explanation: The hostname is perk-check.example. The text before @ is user information.

link-inspector.subject: Design workshop
link-inspector.message: Registration opened for Saturday’s workshop. Your seat is held until tonight.
link-inspector.evidence: https://events.dailybyte.example/workshops/design. The calendar entry on dailybyte.example lists the same link.

actions.label: Open registration
actions.consequence: The confirmed events subdomain shows the workshop.

actions.label: Flag calendar entry
actions.consequence: You flagged a link listed on the official event calendar.

link-inspector.lesson: Read the hostname from the right and use known context. events.dailybyte.example belongs to dailybyte.example.

link-inspector.subject: Member archive
link-inspector.message: A shortcut is available for returning members.

actions.label: Open Member archive
actions.consequence: The address bar shows members-check.example.

actions.label: Find archive from Dailybyte home
actions.consequence: Dailybyte’s own navigation takes you to the archive.

link-inspector.lesson: A brand in the path comes after the hostname. It tells you nothing about who controls the page.

clues.explanation: The brand occurs in the path. The hostname is members-check.example.

spot-the-lookalike.subject: Your files
spot-the-lookalike.message: Sign in to pick up where you left off.

actions.label: Close tab and open bookmark
actions.consequence: Your files open through the saved workspace.

actions.label: Continue in this tab
actions.consequence: The simulated sign-in is hosted on a lookalike with a zero.

spot-the-lookalike.lesson: One swapped letter or digit can change who receives the request.

clues.explanation: A zero replaces the letter o.

spot-the-lookalike.subject: Review your itinerary
spot-the-lookalike.message: Your itinerary has an update. Sign in to view the revised booking.
spot-the-lookalike.evidence: The connection is encrypted. Certificate issued to travel-auth.example. Your saved travel portal is travel.novabyte.example.

actions.label: Continue on the encrypted page
actions.consequence: Encryption protects traffic to travel-auth.example, which is a different service.

actions.label: Open saved Travel portal
actions.consequence: The trusted Novabyte portal shows the itinerary directly.

spot-the-lookalike.lesson: HTTPS secures the connection to the displayed host. It does not vouch for the organization in the page title.

clues.explanation: The hostname belongs to travel-auth.example.

spot-the-lookalike.subject: Reset instructions
spot-the-lookalike.message: You asked for account recovery through the company directory. Here are the instructions.
spot-the-lookalike.evidence: Directory → Account Help: https://help.novabyte.example/reset. The request ID matches your ticket.

actions.label: Read reset instructions
actions.consequence: The known help center shows your requested instructions.

actions.label: Discard as lookalike
actions.consequence: You closed a verified page for an action you initiated.

spot-the-lookalike.lesson: Match the whole hostname and the task you expected. A legitimate subdomain may have an extra label.

double-trouble.subject: Continue to project files
double-trouble.message: You’re switching projects. Confirm your account to open the shared folder.
double-trouble.evidence: Shared link tab: novabyte-login.example/signin. Saved tab: accounts.novabyte.example/signin. The pages use the same logo.

actions.label: Use this tab
actions.consequence: The shared link is outside the company’s domain.

actions.label: Switch to saved sign-in tab
actions.consequence: The known account service shows the project picker.

double-trouble.lesson: Two forms can look identical. Sign in through a saved destination.

clues.explanation: The shared tab uses a different domain.

clues.value: Both tabs show the same logo

double-trouble.subject: Restore session
double-trouble.message: The form is blank. A note suggests copying your saved password manually.
double-trouble.evidence: Your password manager lists accounts.novabyte.example. There’s no match for this page.

actions.label: Leave and open saved sign-in
actions.consequence: Autofill is available on the saved account site.

actions.label: Fill with practice password
actions.consequence: The simulation shows what manual entry would have sent to the lookalike.

double-trouble.lesson: Check the address when a familiar password manager refuses to fill a familiar account.

clues.explanation: The form tries to bypass the password manager’s origin checks.

double-trouble.subject: Approve sign-in?
double-trouble.message: A new one-time code was requested just after you left the lookalike page.
double-trouble.evidence: Current device is already signed in. There’s a pending sign-in from a device you don’t recognize.

actions.label: Approve pending sign-in
actions.consequence: A different simulated device is allowed in.

actions.label: Deny request
actions.consequence: The pending sign-in is rejected.

double-trouble.lesson: Only approve sign-ins you initiated. The timing of a prompt can be part of the setup.

clues.explanation: The attempted login was initiated from another device.

clues.value: Approve a sign-in you didn’t start
clues.explanation: An unsolicited approval can give someone else access.

tick-tock.subject: Access expires in 02:00
tick-tock.message: Confirm your account now to keep access to your saved documents.
tick-tock.evidence: storage.novabyte.example/status → No pending account changes. Last checked just now.

actions.label: Continue in Storage
actions.consequence: Your files are still available through the saved portal.

actions.label: Use Restore access button
actions.consequence: The warning leads to an unrelated account form.

tick-tock.lesson: A countdown changes your attention, not the source. Take time to open the official service yourself.

clues.explanation: The timer pressures you to skip verification.
This domain is separate from the official storage service.

tick-tock.subject: Uploads paused at 18:00
tick-tock.message: Scheduled maintenance starts soon. Leave unfinished uploads in your drafts.
tick-tock.evidence: The company calendar lists the same maintenance window and no sign-in requirement.

actions.label: Flag the maintenance notice
actions.consequence: The notice was legitimate and matched the schedule.

actions.label: Save uploads as drafts
actions.consequence: Your work is saved while the scheduled maintenance begins.

tick-tock.lesson: Real deadlines exist. Verify the context and follow the expected workflow.

tick-tock.subject: One last step
tick-tock.message: Support extended your deadline. Read back the code from your phone to close the request.
tick-tock.evidence: Code purpose: sign in to your workspace from a new browser. It does not authorize support tickets.

actions.label: Share practice code
actions.consequence: The simulated new browser receives an approval code.

actions.label: Report the follow-up
actions.consequence: The support team receives the notice through its normal reporting tool.

tick-tock.lesson: Read the stated purpose of a code. A caller’s description doesn’t change what the code authorizes.

clues.value: Read back the code from your phone
clues.explanation: Support should not request a sign-in code.

clues.value: Sign in from a new browser
clues.explanation: The code authorizes access to the account, not a support step.

download-roulette.subject: invoice.pdf
download-roulette.message: Your monthly invoice is ready to view.
download-roulette.evidence: Full filename: invoice.pdf.exe. File type: Windows executable.

actions.label: Discard file
actions.consequence: The executable is removed from your downloads.

actions.label: Open file
actions.consequence: Opening this file would run a program. The exercise executed nothing.

download-roulette.lesson: The last extension determines the actual type. A filename can contain several dots.

clues.explanation: The last extension is .exe. This can run a program.

download-roulette.subject: Q1-adjustments.xlsm
download-roulette.message: The workbook preview is blank. Click Enable content to see the totals.
download-roulette.evidence: Your finance workflow expects a PDF in the vendor portal. There is no scheduled spreadsheet update.

actions.label: Enable content
actions.consequence: This would allow the workbook to run macros.

actions.label: Request PDF through vendor portal
actions.consequence: The vendor portal provides a plain copy through the established channel.

download-roulette.lesson: A missing preview doesn’t justify running active content. Ask for a safer format through a known channel.

clues.explanation: The file type supports macros.
Enabling content can execute macros.

clues.value: Vendor portal provides an ordinary PDF

download-roulette.subject: reference.pdf
download-roulette.message: The reference sheet you requested is ready.
download-roulette.check: Show file info and request ID
download-roulette.evidence: reference.pdf · PDF document · Request NB-302 matches your portal activity.

actions.label: Open in browser viewer
actions.consequence: The expected PDF opens in the browser viewer.

actions.label: Discard expected PDF
actions.consequence: The file matched the requested document and source.

download-roulette.lesson: Verify source and file type together. A previous suspicious file doesn’t make an independently verified file suspicious.

whos-the-boss.subject: Can you get the vendor paid?
whos-the-boss.message: I’m boarding. Their bank changed this morning. Update the details from my message and let me know once it’s done.
whos-the-boss.evidence: This DM is from an external guest with Avery’s display name. Internal Finance lists a separate account and the formal vendor-change route.

actions.label: Submit change from DM
actions.consequence: The payment workflow uses the unverified bank details.

actions.label: Start verified vendor-change process
actions.consequence: The payment stays paused until the vendor confirms through the established process.

whos-the-boss.lesson: A display name is easy to copy. Payment changes need an independent approval path.

clues.explanation: An external sender copied an internal name.

clues.value: Change bank details from a DM
clues.explanation: The request bypasses the vendor approval workflow.

whos-the-boss.subject: About shipment 5862
whos-the-boss.message: You recognize the voice. The sender knows the shipment number and asks you to keep the request private.
whos-the-boss.evidence: Shipment 5862 appeared on the shared project board yesterday. The number is widely visible.

actions.label: Call Avery from employee directory
actions.consequence: Avery says they didn’t send the voice message.

actions.label: Accept the voice confirmation
actions.consequence: The voice used a public detail that anybody on the project could have copied.

whos-the-boss.lesson: Familiar voice and specific details are weak on their own. Call a number or contact you already trust.

clues.explanation: Secrecy discourages independent verification.

clues.value: Voice recognition is the only proof offered
clues.explanation: A familiar voice cannot establish approval.

whos-the-boss.subject: Vendor change confirmed
whos-the-boss.message: The finance portal shows a reviewed vendor change with an approval record.
whos-the-boss.evidence: Two expected reviewers approved. The vendor callback is logged and matches your established contact.

actions.label: Reject despite approval record
actions.consequence: The expected checks had already verified the update.

actions.label: Release through Finance
actions.consequence: Payment moves through the normal Finance workflow.

whos-the-boss.lesson: Complete a legitimate request once its independent checks are satisfied.

popup-panic.subject: Allow notifications?
popup-panic.message: The page behind the prompt says the video starts after you allow notifications.
popup-panic.evidence: free-movies.example wants notification permission. You only clicked Play.

actions.label: Block notifications
actions.consequence: The site can’t send notifications to your browser.

actions.label: Allow notifications
actions.consequence: The site would be able to send alerts even after you leave the tab.

popup-panic.lesson: Match the requested permission to the action you took. Playback doesn’t need notifications.

clues.explanation: Notifications are unrelated to the Play action.

popup-panic.subject: Allow microphone?
popup-panic.message: You clicked Unmute to speak in the team call you joined from your calendar.
popup-panic.evidence: meet.novabyte.example requests microphone access for the current meeting.

actions.label: Allow for this visit
actions.consequence: Your microphone is available to the expected meeting.

actions.label: Block microphone
actions.consequence: You stay muted because the meeting has no microphone access.

popup-panic.lesson: A permission makes sense when the site, timing, and requested capability match what you intended.

clues.value: Use microphone after you clicked Unmute

popup-panic.subject: Share your screen?
popup-panic.message: The meeting ended. A new tab claims it needs full-screen sharing to upload the recording.
popup-panic.evidence: call-share.example requests the entire screen. The organizer’s meeting page shows no upload request.

actions.label: Share entire screen
actions.consequence: The new origin could view every visible window, not only the meeting.

actions.label: Cancel share
actions.consequence: The new page receives no screen access.

popup-panic.lesson: A context switch and broad access are reasons to stop. Confirm the workflow with the organizer.

clues.explanation: The request came from a different site after the call.
Full-screen sharing exposes all visible windows and is unnecessary here.

clues.value: No upload request in the meeting page

refund-rush.subject: Rs 4,999 credited to A/c XX4321
refund-rush.message: An SMS says Rs 4,999 was credited to your account by UPI. A minute later the same number messages you: “Bhai, I sent 4,999 to the wrong number by mistake. It’s my mother’s hospital fee. Please send it back to 98xxxx4410@okpay, fast.”
refund-rush.evidence: Your Paypocket balance and history show no Rs 4,999 credit. The “bank” SMS came from a personal mobile number.

actions.label: Send Rs 4,999 back
actions.consequence: You sent Rs 4,999 of your own money. Nothing had ever arrived: the SMS was fake.

actions.label: Check my own balance, then tell them to contact their bank
actions.consequence: No credit in your account, so there is nothing to return. A real mistake is fixed by the sender’s bank.

refund-rush.lesson: Trust the balance in your own app, never an SMS or a screenshot. Mistaken transfers are reversed by banks, not by you.

clues.explanation: Banks send credit alerts from short sender IDs like AX-BANKNM, not a personal phone number.

clues.value: Paypocket balance: unchanged, no Rs 4,999 credit
clues.explanation: The only proof that matters is your own account. It shows nothing arrived.

clues.value: “Hospital fee, please send it back fast”
clues.explanation: An emotional story plus a rush is there to stop you checking.

refund-rush.subject: Approve to receive your Rs 4,999 refund
refund-rush.message: The same person writes: “No problem, I raised a refund for you. Just approve the request and enter your PIN to receive it.” A Paypocket request appears: Refund Desk, Rs 4,999. Enter UPI PIN to approve.
refund-rush.evidence: It is a collect request. Approving it pays Rs 4,999 from your account to refunddesk@okpocket.

actions.label: Enter PIN to receive the refund
actions.consequence: Rs 4,999 left your account. A UPI PIN is only ever used to send money.

actions.label: Decline the request and block the sender
actions.consequence: Nothing leaves your account, and they can’t send you more requests.

refund-rush.lesson: You never enter a UPI PIN to receive money. A PIN means money is going out.

clues.value: Type: collect request (pay from your account)
clues.explanation: Receiving money never needs your approval or PIN. A collect request takes money out.
The screen says debit: the money goes out, not in.
A “refund desk” with a brand-new personal UPI ID is not a real support team.

refund-rush.subject: Return the money or face a police case
refund-rush.message: This time Rs 8,000 really did arrive, from someone called Kiran S. you don’t know. A caller says he is from the cyber cell: the money was sent by mistake, and you must move it to a “safe account” within 30 minutes or your account will be frozen and a case filed.
refund-rush.evidence: The Rs 8,000 credit is real, from an account you don’t know. The caller wants it sent to a different UPI ID, not back to the sender.

actions.label: Transfer Rs 8,000 to the account he gives
actions.consequence: If the money came from a hacked account, you just helped move stolen money, and your account is now in the trail.

actions.label: Send nothing. Tell your bank and call 1930
actions.consequence: Your bank reverses a genuine mistake through official channels. 1930 is India’s national cybercrime helpline.

refund-rush.lesson: Real money from a stranger is the most dangerous kind. Don’t move it yourself: let your bank reverse it, and report pressure calls to 1930.

clues.value: Caller says he’s “Inspector Rao, Cyber Cell”
clues.explanation: Police don’t phone you to ask for transfers. Anyone can claim a title on a call.
A genuine return goes back to the sender through the bank, never to a new “safe” account.

clues.value: “Within 30 minutes, or your account is frozen”
clues.explanation: Threats and deadlines are pressure, not procedure.
